edges.description: Reduced rotatin impairs assembly of full-length centrioles.
Defective centrioles disrupt spindle-pole formation in mitosis.
edges.target: Mitotic Spindle Dysfunction and Centrosome Amplification

edges.description: Mitotic failure leads to aneuploidy and apoptosis of dividing neural progenitors.
edges.source: Mitotic Spindle Dysfunction and Centrosome Amplification

edges.description: Loss of the proliferative progenitor pool reduces cortical neuron number.
Impaired ciliary cortical-patterning signalling is proposed to drive abnormal cortical organization.
Impaired neuronal migration produces a simplified/thickened cortex.
Arrest of migrating neurons produces periventricular heterotopia.
Reproduces the aneuploidy, cell-cycle arrest and death of neural stem cells and the delayed neural-rosette self-organization that underlie microcephaly.
edges.limitations: Organoids lack the full in-vivo cortical architecture and vascular/immune context; the model captures progenitor-level defects rather than the complete malformation.
edges.source: CRISPR iPSC-derived neural stem cells and cortical organoids (RTTN c.2953A>G)

edges.description: Establishes that rotatin is essential in development, but the null allele models neither the human cortical phenotype nor the partial-loss-of-function mechanism of the human disease.
edges.limitations: This is a null allele, whereas human disease is caused by hypomorphic (partial-loss-of-function) alleles with residual rotatin activity; the complete loss is embryonic-lethal in the mouse with randomized heart looping and failed axial rotation, a phenotype patients do not show, so the null mouse does not reproduce the human microcephaly/cortical disease.

nodes.description: CRISPR/Cas9-edited iPSC differentiated into neural stem cells and cortical organoids carrying the recurrent p.Arg985Gly allele.
nodes.id: CRISPR iPSC-derived neural stem cells and cortical organoids (RTTN c.2953A>G)

nodes.description: Rotatin localizes to the basal body and ciliary axoneme; loss produces structural cilia abnormalities and downregulation of BMP4, WNT5A and WNT2B, key regulators of cortical patterning. This branch is proposed to underlie the cortical organization defects (polymicrogyria). The link to the human cortical phenotype is inferred from fibroblast findings.

evidence.reference_title: RTTN mutations link primary cilia function to organization of the human cerebral cortex.
evidence.snippet: Cultured fibroblasts from affected individuals have structural abnormalities of the cilia and exhibit downregulation of BMP4, WNT5A, and WNT2B, which are key regulators of cortical patterning

nodes.description: Rotatin acts downstream of STIL-mediated procentriole initiation and is required to build full-length centrioles; it recruits CEP295 and the distal-centriole proteins POC5/POC1B and forms a complex with PPP1R35. Loss of rotatin produces short or incomplete centrioles.

evidence.reference_title: Human microcephaly protein RTTN interacts with STIL and is required to build full-length centrioles.
evidence.snippet: Further studies demonstrate that RTTN directly interacts with STIL and acts downstream of STIL-mediated centriole assembly.

evidence.reference_title: PPP1R35 is a novel centrosomal protein that regulates centriole length in concert with the microcephaly protein RTTN.
evidence.snippet: We further demonstrate that PPP1R35 acts downstream of, and forms a complex with, RTTN, a microcephaly protein required for distal centriole elongation.

nodes.description: Rotatin localizes to the leading-edge centrosome of migrating iPSC-derived neurons and interacts with non-muscle myosin heavy chains, the motors of nucleokinesis during neuronal migration. Loss of this function is proposed to cause defective migration, producing lissencephaly/pachygyria and heterotopia. Inferred from localization and interaction data.

evidence.reference_title: Heterogeneous clinical phenotypes and cerebral malformations reflected by rotatin cellular dynamics.
evidence.snippet: rotatin interacts with the neuronal (non-muscle) myosin heavy chain subunits, motors of nucleokinesis during neuronal migration, and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived bipolar mature neurons rotatin localizes at the centrosome in the leading edge.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic mutations in RTTN are associated with microcephaly, short stature and a wide range of brain malformations.
evidence.snippet: The phenotype consisted of microcephaly, short stature, pachygyria or polymicrogyria, colpocephaly, hypoplasia of the corpus callosum and superior vermis.

nodes.description: Defective centrioles cause centrosome amplification, dispersion of pericentriolar gamma-tubulin, and monopolar/multipolar spindles with misorientation, producing mitotic failure in dividing cells, including patient fibroblasts.
nodes.id: Mitotic Spindle Dysfunction and Centrosome Amplification

evidence.reference_title: Human Microcephaly Protein RTTN Is Required for Proper Mitotic Progression and Correct Spindle Position.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that RTTN is required for normal mitotic progression and correct spindle position.

evidence.reference_title: Heterogeneous clinical phenotypes and cerebral malformations reflected by rotatin cellular dynamics.
evidence.snippet: Mutant cells showed consistent and severe mitotic failure with centrosome amplification and multipolar spindle formation, leading to aneuploidy and apoptosis, which could relate to depletion of neuronal progenitors often observed in microcephaly.

nodes.description: Mitotic failure produces aneuploidy, cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis of neural stem and progenitor cells, depleting the proliferative pool and the radial glial scaffold during cortical neurogenesis. Shown in CRISPR-edited iPSC-derived neural stem cells and cortical organoids.

evidence.reference_title: A Taybi-Linder syndrome-related RTTN variant impedes neural rosette formation in human cortical organoids.
evidence.snippet: we analysed neural stem cells (NSC) derived from CRISPR/Cas9-edited induced pluripotent stem cells and revealed major cell cycle and mitotic abnormalities, leading to aneuploidy, cell cycle arrest and cell death.

evidence.reference_title: Radial Microbrain (Micrencephaly) Is Caused by a Recurrent Variant in the RTTN Gene.
evidence.snippet: The cortical plate was reduced by 70% compared with controls, irrespective of the region considered. Immunostaining with vimentin showed a 50% loss of radial glial columns, characteristic of radial microbrain.

experimental_models.description: Reproduces the aneuploidy, cell-cycle arrest and death of neural stem cells and the delayed neural-rosette self-organization that underlie microcephaly.
experimental_models.name: CRISPR iPSC-derived neural stem cells and cortical organoids (RTTN c.2953A>G)

evidence.reference_title: Heterogeneous clinical phenotypes and cerebral malformations reflected by rotatin cellular dynamics.
evidence.snippet: the core phenotype, consisting of intellectual disability, short stature, microcephaly, lissencephaly, periventricular heterotopia, polymicrogyria and other malformations.

evidence.reference_title: RTTN mutations link primary cilia function to organization of the human cerebral cortex.
evidence.snippet: We have identified autosomal-recessive mutations in RTTN, encoding Rotatin, in individuals with bilateral diffuse polymicrogyria from two separate families.

evidence.reference_title: RTTN Mutations Cause Primary Microcephaly and Primordial Dwarfism in Humans.
evidence.snippet: Our results expand the phenotype of RTTN-related disorders, hitherto limited to polymicrogyria, to include microcephalic primordial dwarfism with a complex brain phenotype involving simplified gyration.

evidence.reference_title: RTTN Mutations Cause Primary Microcephaly and Primordial Dwarfism in Humans.
evidence.snippet: Our results expand the phenotype of RTTN-related disorders, hitherto limited to polymicrogyria, to include microcephalic primordial dwarfism with a complex brain phenotype involving simplified gyration.

evidence.reference_title: Recurrent RTTN mutation leading to severe microcephaly, polymicrogyria and growth restriction.
evidence.snippet: We identified, by trio based whole exome sequencing, a homozygous missense mutation in the RTTN gene (c.2953A > G; p.(Arg985Gly)) in one Moroccan patient from a consanguineous family.

nodes.description: Biallelic hypomorphic RTTN variants reduce or mislocalize rotatin, a centriolar scaffold protein. The severity of the disorder tracks the residual function of the protein rather than the mRNA level.

animal_models.description: Establishes that rotatin is essential in development, but the null allele models neither the human cortical phenotype nor the partial-loss-of-function mechanism of the human disease.
animal_models.name: Rttn knockout mouse (axial-rotation / no-turning)

evidence.reference_title: Heterogeneous clinical phenotypes and cerebral malformations reflected by rotatin cellular dynamics.
evidence.snippet: We show that the severity of the phenotype is related to residual function of the protein, not only the level of mRNA expression.

nodes.description: The founding rotatin mouse allele; null embryos fail axial rotation and show laterality defects and embryonic lethality.
Recurrent homozygous missense variant (NM_173630) that also alters the exon 23 splice-donor site; reported in North African/Moroccan consanguineous families and recurrent in radial microbrain.
Homozygous splice-site variant causing skipping of exon 42 and a C-terminal frameshift; associated with stationary disease into the seventh decade and brachydactyly.
Naturally occurring microcephaly-associated missense variant that shows low affinity for STIL binding and blocks centriole assembly.
